Vivek / team — draft language below. Kept it intentionally concise to make it easy to paste into Exhibit B: Pricing Schedule.

1) Tail Smoothing Credit (dynamic)
"If, in any billing month during the Term, Customer's billable usage in tokens (\"Monthly Usage\") is less than seventy percent (70%) of the Customer's three-month rolling average Monthly Usage (the \"Rolling Average\"), Customer shall be entitled to a Tail Smoothing Credit equal to the difference between (a) the charge that would have applied based on the Rolling Average and (b) the actual charge for the Monthly Usage, calculated using the rates in the Order Form. The Rolling Average shall be calculated as the arithmetic mean of the Monthly Usage for the three months immediately preceding the month subject to calculation. For clarity, 'Committed Monthly Throughput' shall mean the monthly token commitment specified in Schedule A of the Order Form."

2) Minimum Commitment Option (fixed)
"Customer may elect, in writing, to set a Minimum Monthly Commitment for the Term, which shall be 70% of the Committed Monthly Throughput unless otherwise agreed in writing (the 'Minimum Commitment'). Charges for any month where Monthly Usage is below the Minimum Commitment shall be invoiced at the Minimum Commitment level and reconciled quarterly against actual usage; any shortfall amounts shall be credited at the time of reconciliation unless otherwise agreed."

Legal notes:
- I used 70% as the baseline language (i.e., 30% buffer). If you want to show the 40% option, we can create a parallel clause with 60% (i.e., 40% buffer).
- For spike ceiling, I recommend we accept '1.5x Committed Monthly Throughput' as a short-term ceiling and include a reconciliation mechanism that allows excess usage to be billed at the listed overage rate, subject to post-quarter true-up.

Ben — if you can add worked examples (numbers) below the clauses for 30% and 40% scenarios, we can include both in the counter-redline.

Neha Kapoor
